value.locator: PDF p2, §II-B, Fig2b, request watcher/CSHR issue and metadata paragraphs
value.statement: One active CSHR accepts hits in parallel. Pending misses cause its current wide access and hitmap/offset metadata to issue; misses determine next tag. After all window requests coalesce, the regulator advances; a watchdog can issue the current block when no new window arrives.
limitations: Publication mechanism only; public realization/commit, concrete ID lifetime, backpressure and complete transaction ABI remain independently unbound.

value.description: Each TU has equal-sized circular data streams advanced together. fite stalls when streams are full, preserves parent element ordinal association, and emits iteration/end control tokens. No physical response-tag/slot protocol follows from logical queue association.

TUs in one lane share storage. Configuration allocates the same stream count and size to TUs within a layer, with shorter leftward queues and more storage for rightward parallel loops; an analytical sizing model uses estimated nnzs per fiber. This is not a complete legal sizing domain.

TG output construction and the thread-private outQ are double-buffered so the CPU handles a full chunk while the TMU supplies another. The chunk size, last partial-chunk transfer and consumption/reuse handshake are not specified.

TG output FSM construction is serialized across groups, with wait-for-previous/next states preserving CPU callback/operand sequence while traversal and merging can proceed independently. This does not assert memory-response FIFO or global memory order.

Issue cacheline-granularity accesses by prioritizing leftmost outer-loop layers, selecting TUs round-robin within a layer, then streams in configuration order and requests in each queue in order. No general fairness bound, CAM duplicate suppression or response ordering is established.

fbeg waits for valid parent bounds; fite generates streams from the corresponding parent element. In Fig8 row-pointer heads initialize two offset0/1 stride2 lanes; column indexes feed dependent b lookups while nnz values remain aligned by element ordinal.

TG considers a lane active only under its parent predicate and gite waits for valid active heads. Fig8 LockStep consumes active unfinished lanes and emits end when all finish. General conjunctive/disjunctive modes are source context only, not new operations admitted for this mapping. Padding/msk validity and empty/odd-row handling remain requirements.

Fig8 GITE produces ri with paired nnz and vector values; GEND produces re. CPU ri performs multiply/vector reduction/accumulation; CPU re writes the row result and resets sum. Hardware operand supply is neither generic standalone gather execution nor TMU arithmetic/scatter. Numerical order/equivalence belongs to the CPU mapping.

GEND supplies the mapped row-end callback and a full outQ chunk becomes CPU work while the alternate chunk fills. This logical supply boundary does not establish final-partial delivery, consumed acknowledgment, CPU output visibility or all outstanding physical-request drain.

Traversal uses coherent read-only data from LLC; thread-private outQ is injected into the core private L2. Virtual addresses use host L2 TLB/MMU; missing translation interrupts the core and the MMU signals retry. The stated no-shared-read-write-data regime does not cover arbitrary aliases/concurrent mutation.

Context switching quiesces TMU and saves/restores initial configuration, ite stream heads, outQ base/write offset and other control registers. Exact request cancellation, response drain, exception sequencing and replay protocol are not established.

Table5 reports8 lanes,4 TGs with mergers,2KB per-lane storage and128 outstanding requests for the evaluated system. Fig8 instead illustrates2 lanes. These values remain fixed references, not legal capacity ranges, a selected new geometry or a bit-width ABI.

bininit establishes per-level reserved/used ways, unique-index domain, tuple size and bin range before binupdate selects a C-Buffer. Per-thread bin counts/starting offsets and an unnamed LLC offset initialization instruction supply memory destinations. Full-buffer offset advances and residual binflush must complete before software Accumulate consumes bins; no destination-update executor or generic FP reorder permission is implied.

The single active CSHR accepts matching valid window entries and retains tag/hitmap/offset metadata. Pending misses cause its current wide block to issue and metadata to enqueue, while misses select the next tag. Completion of a window allows another window; a separate watchdog issues a pending block if no new window arrives. Metadata backpressure and exact transaction/ID reuse need concrete implementation binding.
